title: Where is it?
goal: Ask and explain where things and places are, using place words like ondoan and aurrean, and say that something is or isn't there.
bekal: use *-ren ondoan, aurrean, atzean, gainean, azpian, artean*
tell *dago* (one) from *daude* (several), and *badago* (there is) from *ez dago* (there isn't)
name common places in town and ask a stranger where they are

dialogs.title: Elkarrizketa — Galduta Bilbon
dialogs.intro: Budi stops in a small square and asks a woman who is waiting for the bus.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: Excuse me, where is the Guggenheim Museum?

lines.speaker: Emakumea:
lines.text: Museoa ibaiaren ondoan dago, hemendik hurbil.
lines.id: The museum is by the river, close to here.
lines.literal: museum-the river-of side-at is, here-from near.

lines.speaker: Emakumea:
lines.text: Ez, hamar minutu. Zuzen joan eta gero ezkerrera.
lines.id: No, ten minutes. Go straight and then left.
lines.literal: no, ten minute. straight go and then left-to.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Eskerrik asko. Eta banketxe bat, hemen inguruan?
lines.id: Thank you. And is there a bank around here?
lines.literal: thanks many. and bank one, here around-at?

lines.speaker: Emakumea:
lines.text: Bai, kale honen amaieran dago, farmaziaren aurrean.
lines.id: Yes, at the end of this street, in front of the pharmacy.
lines.literal: yes, street this-of end-at is, pharmacy-of front-at.

lines.speaker: Emakumea:
lines.text: Ez dakit. Normalean zortzietatik zortzietara irekita egoten da.
lines.id: I don't know. It's usually open from eight to eight.
lines.literal: not I-know. normally eight-pl-from eight-pl-to open being is.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: Good. And where are the restrooms?

lines.speaker: Emakumea:
lines.id: In the square, behind the fountain.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: Thanks a lot! You're very kind.

notes: **Place words need -ren in front of them.** *Ibaia**ren** ondoan* (next to the river), *farmazia**ren** aurrean* (in front of the pharmacy). The pattern: reference object + *-ren* + place word + *-an*. English puts it the other way round — "next to the river" — so get used to flipping the order in your head.

**Dago for one, daude for several.** *Museoa hemen **dago*** (the museum is here), *komunak han **daude*** (the restrooms are over there). Native speakers notice this mistake right away, and it's easy to avoid once you get used to spotting *-ak* at the end of the noun.

**Mila esker — a warmer way to say thanks.** It literally means "a thousand thanks". From shortest to warmest: *eskerrik asko* < *mila esker* < *eskerrik asko bihotzez* ("thank you from the heart"). All are answered with *ez horregatik* or *ez dago zergatik*.

**Irekita and itxita describe a state, so they take egon.** *Irekita **dago*** (it's open), *itxita **dago*** (it's closed). These are the *-ta* words you met in Unit 10, and they always pair with *egon*, never with *izan*.

blocks.text: All of these are really ordinary nouns with the place ending *-an*: *gain* (top surface) → *gainean* (on its top). That's why they need an owner in front, and the owner is marked with *-ren* — just like "the table's top".

blocks.title: Three direction endings to keep apart
items: **-an** = at/in (staying there): *etxean nago* — I'm at home.
**-ra** = to (heading there): *etxera noa* — I'm going home.
**-tik** = from (coming from): *etxetik nator* — I'm coming from home.
All three also work with place words: *mahaiaren gainean* (on the table), *mahaiaren gainera* (onto the table), *mahaiaren gainetik* (off the table).

blocks.text: To say something is or isn't somewhere, Basque uses *egon* — the same verb as "to be (located)".

head: Euskara
Literally
English
rows: How many students are in the class?

blocks.text: Notice the ending *-rik* again in negative sentences: *ez dago banketxe**rik***. The same rule you learned in Unit 5 for objects applies here too.

blocks.title: Four "no-" words
items: *inoiz ez* — never. *Ez naiz inoiz Parisen egon.*
All four always pair with *ez* — the negation is said twice, like "not … anybody" in English.

blocks.text: Notice the ending *-tegi*, meaning "place for": *liburu**tegi*** (book place = library), *euskal**tegi*** (Basque-language school), *sagardo**tegi*** (cider house), *ostatu*. And *-etxe*, meaning "house": *jat**etxe**a* (eating house = restaurant), *udal**etxe**a* (town-council house), *bank**etxe**a*.

blocks.title: Asking for directions
items: *Barkatu, non dago …?* — Excuse me, where is …?
*Hemendik hurbil dago?* — Is it close to here?
*Berriro esan, mesedez.* — Say it again, please.
